questions.def: Tasteless is an ungradable adjective and cannot be used with 'more'.
questions.question: This soup is very ___. I need more salt.

questions.def: Fantastic is an ungradable adjective, so 'more' is incorrect.
questions.question: This movie is more fantastic than I expected.

questions.def: Delicious is gradable so we do not need a modifier
questions.question: The cake was ___. Everyone loved it.

questions.def: Cold is a gradable adjective, so 'very' is the correct modifier.
questions.question: The weather is ___ cold today. I need a coat.

questions.def: Certain is an ungradable adjective and 'absolutely' is the correct modifier.
questions.question: I am ___ certain that I locked the door.

questions.def: Perfect is ungradable, so it doesn't need a modifier.
questions.question: The weather for the picnic was ___.

questions.def: 'Very' correctly modifies the gradable adjective 'tired'.
questions.question: She was ___ tired after the long day.

questions.def: 'Quite' is appropriate for describing a gradable adjective.
questions.question: The exam was ___ difficult.

questions.def: Hungry is gradable and needs no modifier on its own.
questions.question: I'm ___. Can we get something to eat?

questions.def: 'Interesting' is gradable, so 'very' is the correct modifier.
questions.question: The presentation was ___ interesting.

questions.def: 'Sure' is ungradable; 'absolutely' is the correct modifier.
questions.question: I am ___ sure I turned off the lights.

questions.def: Frightened is gradable, so no modifier is needed.
questions.question: The child was ___ by the loud noise.

questions.def: 'Funny' is gradable, so we use 'very' to modify it.
questions.question: The movie was ___ funny. I laughed a lot.

questions.def: 'Exhausted' is ungradable; 'absolutely' is the correct modifier.
questions.question: He is ___ exhausted after the marathon.

questions.def: Cold is gradable, so 'cold' on its own is acceptable.
questions.question: It's ___ outside. Wear a jacket.

questions.def: 'Beautiful' is gradable; 'very' is a good modifier.
questions.question: She is ___ beautiful.

questions.def: 'Finished' is ungradable here; 'completely' is correct.
questions.question: I am ___ finished with my work.

questions.def: Angry is gradable, we can use it without a modifier.
questions.question: He was ___ when he found out.

questions.def: 'Big' is gradable, so 'very' is a correct modifier.
questions.question: The house is ___ big.

questions.def: 'Certain' is ungradable; 'absolutely' is the correct modifier.
questions.question: I am ___ certain about my answer.

questions.def: Hot is gradable, so no modifier is needed here.
questions.question: The coffee is ___. Be careful.

questions.def: 'Easy' is gradable; 'very' is an appropriate modifier.
questions.question: The test was ___ easy.

questions.def: 'Dead' is ungradable; 'absolutely' is the proper modifier.
questions.question: He is ___ dead.

questions.def: Delicious is a gradable adjective, so we use 'very'.
questions.question: This soup is ___ delicious.

questions.def: Tired is gradable. 'Too' indicates more than enough.
questions.question: I am ___ tired to go out tonight.

questions.def: 'Happy' is gradable; use 'very' instead of 'much'.
questions.question: She is much happy to see you again.

questions.def: 'Spotless' is ungradable, so use 'completely'.
questions.question: The house is ___ spotless after she finished.

questions.def: Awful is ungradable, so we use 'absolutely'.
questions.question: The movie was ___ awful.

questions.def: Certain is ungradable. Use 'completely' to modify it.
questions.question: He is ___ certain about his answer.
